headline: Majors pinned below 200-day lines while funding stays expensive and whales pull coins off-exchange.
paragraphs: The entire major cohort sits below the 200-day simple moving average: Bitcoin at 63,747 has no golden cross, Ethereum at 1,895 is well below trend, and six of seven tracked assets are in the same posture. This is the regime. Bitcoin has posted 0.33% in 24 hours and 0.44% over seven days, while Ethereum moved 0.8% and 0.74% respectively. Month-to-date tells a different story: Bitcoin up 8.85%, Ethereum up 20.75%. The rally is real but it is happening inside a downtrend, which is a contradiction worth holding. Bitcoin sits 48.9% below its 12-month high of 124,739; Ethereum is 60.7% below 4,817. The 90-day range shows Bitcoin moved from 58,566 to 79,068, so today's price is in the upper half of recent trading but nowhere near escape velocity.

Momentum and trend are not aligned. Bitcoin's RSI-14 is 47.6 (neutral, neither overbought nor oversold) and MACD sits below signal, meaning the 30-day move into positive territory has not yet sustained momentum on the derivative. Ethereum's RSI is 53.2 with MACD also below signal, identical posture. Contrast this with Solana, where RSI is 53.7 and MACD is above signal, a small bullish divergence against the fact that SOL remains below its 200-day line and 69.3% below its 12-month peak. BNB shows RSI at 65.7, the only major approaching overbought territory, paired with MACD above signal, yet BNB is still below trend and 53.1% off the high. The message is that upward momentum is present in pockets and intact on some technical reads, but it is not yet validating the longer trend. This is the posture of a rally that has legs but not yet confirmation.

Funding costs on leverage are elevated across most majors, which rewards long holders but signals comfort with the long side. Bitcoin perpetual funding at OKX is 0.0054% per 8 hours, annualizing to 5.9%. Ethereum is 0.0069% per 8 hours, annualizing to 7.5%. XRP and DOGE are both above 9% annualized, and SOL is negative at minus 3.4%, meaning shorts are being paid to hold. Bitcoin open interest stands at 2.04 billion USD with a long-to-short ratio of 1.59 (longs outnumber shorts by 59%), Ethereum at 1.30 billion with a 1.42 ratio. The extreme imbalance sits in XRP at 3.35 to 1 and DOGE at 4.21 to 1, assets trading at multiyear lows with four times more long contracts than short. Over the last 24 hours, Bitcoin liquidations have been heavily skewed to the long side: 7.26 million in long liquidations against 1.39 million in shorts, a ratio of 5.2 to 1. This suggests leverage is being shaken out on rallies.

Whale flows reveal active repositioning. Over the past 48 hours, 82.7 million USD has moved off exchanges in net terms, led by Ethereum withdrawals of 56.2 million and Bitcoin withdrawals of 26.6 million. The biggest single move was 169.9 million in USDT leaving Bitfinex, alongside 128.9 million in Bitcoin exiting Kraken and 73.5 million exiting OKEx. At the same time, 90.3 million in Bitcoin moved onto Coinbase Institutional and 66.5 million onto Coinbase standard. The pattern is: stablecoins moving away from lending venues (Bitfinex), major assets moving to self-custody or cold storage, and a competing flow into regulated US institutional access. The five-week trend is volatile but directional: last week was minus 741 million off-exchange, the week before that plus 1.17 billion on-exchange, showing whales are not building a consistent conviction into either posture. Stablecoin float sits at 306.4 billion USD, down 0.98% over 30 days, a modest contraction in dry powder.

Sentiment stands at 27 (Fear) with a 30-day range of 22 to 33, meaning the needle has barely moved off its lows. The disconnect is important: while the crowd's gauge remains in fear, on-chain flows show large holders pulling assets into self-custody, which is an action of relative confidence, not panic. Bitcoin and Ethereum ETF flows tell a similar story of mismatch. Bitcoin received 7.8 million USD on 11 August but 346.9 million over the last five sessions, with only one day in the same direction. Ethereum received minus 1.7 million on the latest day but plus 186.2 million over five sessions. This is the institutional bid persisting despite short-term chop.

Watch for three conditions: the first is whether Bitcoin or Ethereum can reclaim their 200-day moving averages while funding remains elevated, which would signal the downtrend is ending rather than pausing. The second is the long liquidation ratio in Bitcoin and Ethereum leverage. A flip toward short liquidations would suggest longs are becoming less fragile. Third is whether whale accumulation into cold storage continues or reverses back toward exchanges, as that flow shift is the real tell of where large capital intends to hold positions. The 90-day range and the funding costs give the setup room, but trend confirmation is missing.
